title: Governance gates — promotion is slow, demotion is fast
description: The lifecycle gates that sit above the performance gates (G-1..G-13). G-16 is the demotion gate the brief mandates: a live strategy that degrades goes back to PAPER, not to a meeting. Promotion on signal only; demotion on either signal decay or risk breach; staking outcomes can never promote.

rows.scope: any strategy at Stage 3 (live trial) or Stage 4 (funded)
rows.trigger_a_signal_decay: rolling 250-bet closing-line-value lower bound < 0 at two consecutive monthly evaluations, OR signal ROI below break-even over the trailing 150 settled bets with the one-sided test p > 0.5 (indistinguishable from losing)
rows.trigger_b_risk_breach: drawdown from live peak exceeds 50% of allocated bankroll at live stakes, OR stake cap exceeded, OR a ledger audit invalidates settled results (source correction)
rows.trigger_c_compliance: any G-12 failure (prohibited market class, unregistered input, non-public information) — immediate, no evaluation window
rows.destination: PAPER (Stage 2 exposure): zero capital, sealed evaluation continues, the entry keeps its record and its graveyard rights
rows.execution: automatic at the evaluation checkpoint by the system; no discretion, no appeal; the demotion event is written to the strategy's sealed log
rows.re_entry: back through the normal ladder from paper: a fresh sealed window of >= 150 settled paper bets with positive CLV lower bound AND all hard gates re-cleared on that window; a demoted strategy may not re-enter live on the strength of its old record
rows.asymmetry_rule: staking outcomes can NEVER promote (promotion reads signal columns only), but a staking risk breach CAN demote. A lucky staking run masks nothing; a dangerous one is punished.
rows.why: The failure mode of every strategy programme is the edge that died quietly while the bankroll looked fine. G-11 monitors decay; G-16 is the enforcement: the strategy stops carrying capital the moment the evidence stops supporting it.

rows.rule: rank order, reward eligibility and capital promotion are computed from the SIGNAL ledger (flat stakes: hit rate, CLV/edge, flat ROI, gates, LCB). The STAKING ledger is published as risk telemetry beside it and can only cap or remove exposure. A strategy whose staking run is positive while its signal is not is displayed with the MASKED flag and is not eligible for promotion.
rows.implementation: data/signal_vs_staking.csv (scripts/build_signal_staking_m.py); signal_rank is computed without any staking column entering the sort
rows.why: so a lucky staking run cannot mask a bad signal

notes: G-16 demotion is defined at the strategy level; a division-level circuit breaker (all live entries failing together) is deliberately NOT in v1 and is listed as a suggestion for review.
Every trigger metric here is computable from the sealed bet log plus the price-snapshot store; none of them require judgment calls at execution time.
